title: Moral Advice as Interactional Negotiation: Framing, User Pressure, and Social Position in Large Language Model Responses

bias_targets.methodology: Tracking conversational accommodation by measuring whether and when the LLM shifts its initial moral stance to align with successive rounds of user disagreement across a multi-turn protocol.
Using a factorial vignette experiment to compare LLM baseline moral judgments and accommodation trajectories for eldercare dilemmas when the persona is specified as male, female, or undisclosed.
Varying the sibling configuration of the persona (e.g., only child, oldest with sisters, oldest with brothers) to assess how expectations of caregiving alter the model's moral evaluations.
Evaluating differences in LLM moral advice and resistance to user pushback across different specified persona age brackets (18-30, 30-45, 45-60, 60 or above).

Testing how LLM moral evaluations and accommodation timing change based on the persona's educational attainment (no college degree vs. college degree or above) and geographic region (urban vs. rural).
